_schema._comment: SCHEMA OF THIS FILE. JSON has no comments, so this block is the documentation. Update it every time the data schema changes (Adi, 2026-10-18) and add a changelog line.
_schema.one_record_per: jurisdiction (city, or county for unincorporated land); 28 records; the engine's single setback record per jurisdiction — research with quotes lives INSIDE the field it supports, not in sibling files

record_fields.jurisdiction: display name; counties carry the suffix ' (unincorporated)'
record_fields.slug: kebab-case id, same as corpus/<slug>/ and the other research files (e.g. san-mateo-county)
record_fields.ordinance_link: URL of the published ADU ordinance. Published = in effect (Adi 2026-09-23): no status lookup, and HCD review letters are not a source
record_fields.code_platform: Municode | eCode360 | Zoneomics code viewer (Zoneomics hosts the code text itself) | ... — tells the corpus pipeline how to scrape
record_fields.zoneomics_city_name / zoneomics_city_id: provenance of ordinance_link: Zoneomics v2/zoneDetail, queried 2026-08-27 at one representative point per city. The five county records (added 2026-08-30) have no city_id: their links come from direct county-code research

front_rule.what: how the jurisdiction decides which edge of a multi-street lot is the FRONT; consumed by the edge labeler (edge-labeling/edge-labeling.ts, gaudi-api-port/services/parcel_data/front_rules.py)
front_rule.rule: address_street | shortest_frontage | designated | owner_elected | all_fronts. Engine default for an unlisted jurisdiction: address_street (the street in the situs address), falling back to shortest frontage
front_rule.source: 'code' = verified in the municipal code, see citation
front_rule.citation: code section + the sentence it rests on
front_rule.overrides: optional list of {rule, condition, citation, description, zone_codes?}: conditions under which a different rule applies (San Jose: oversized corner lots and pedestrian districts are all_fronts). An unevaluable condition falls back silently to address_street
front_rule.engine_rule: a street_side edge is a side (state 4 ft cap) unless the rule is all_fronts, where the second frontage is a front (Adi 2026-09-23)

residential_front_setback.what: the jurisdiction's ZONING-DISTRICT front setback for housing, in feet (city or county). Used as the state-track front whenever state_track_front.rule == 'district' (counsel 2026-09-24: Gov. Code § 66323(a)(2) sets side and rear only), and as the local-track front
residential_front_setback.by_district: {zone code: feet} from the code table, matched against the parcel's zone code (case and punctuation ignored); empty when the jurisdiction has one value
residential_front_setback.source / citation / extracted / corpus_d: 'code' + the section; extracted 2026-09-24 from corpus/<slug>/sf-district-standards.txt; note = caveats (block averages, contextual rules)

state_track_front.what: what the jurisdiction's OWN ADU chapter says about the front setback of the state-track unit (Gov. Code § 66323(a)(2), ≤ 800 sf). Decision Adi 2026-10-18 (FOR-1511): the engine describes what the lot has BY RIGHT
state_track_front.rule: 'local' = the chapter sets its own front for this unit → the engine takes value_ft. 'district' = use residential_front_setback. FOR-1511 scope: only the six classification == grant_local records are 'local'
state_track_front.value_ft: the chapter's own front value when rule == 'local' (0 ft in all six today; the engine reads the number, it never assumes 0); null otherwise
state_track_front.value_rule: formula for a lot-specific local value, or null. San Mateo County: min(district_front_ft, primary_front_distance_ft) — deferred until the primary footprint exists (rule stays 'district' + flag)
state_track_front.flags: flags the engine must raise: front_from_local_adu_chapter (rule local) · front_local_grant_by_disapplication (Napa: the chapter switches its front clause off for § 66323(a) units) · front_rule_mixed (Healdsburg, San Carlos) · front_rule_silent (10 chapters, pending counsel) · front_rule_needs_primary_footprint (San Mateo County)
state_track_front.classification: reading of the local text, 28-chapter pass 2026-10-18: grant_local 6 (chapter sets its own front for this unit; 'no front setback' in all six) · conditional_yield 9 (zoning front applies but yields if it would preclude an 800 sf unit — case-by-case at the counter, NOT by right) · district_applies 1 (Santa Clara County, no relief) · silent 10 (the unit's section lists side/rear/size/height only; the chapter disapplies its own standards for it and names no front) · mixed 2 (an unconditional clause and a conditional one in the same chapter)
state_track_front.threshold_sf: the chapter's own small-unit threshold (800 in most; Fairfax Class 1 runs to 1,200; Healdsburg's state-mandated unit to 850)
state_track_front.citation / quote / placement_rule / note: verbatim quote with its section; placement_rule = any rule keeping the unit out of the front yard even without a front setback ({exists, quote, citation, exempted_by_notwithstanding}); notes = hard calls and the engine-scope note; source = corpus doc read + ticket

file_fields.title / generated / source / count: provenance of the original 2026-08-27 Zoneomics export; count = number of records

state_track_front.quote: [6-564(a)] Limited Detached on Single-family Lot: One detached, new-construction ADU on a lot with a proposed or existing single-family dwelling (in addition to any JADU that might be established on the lot), if the detached ADU satisfies all of the following limitations: (1) The side- and rear-yard setbacks are at least four feet. (2) The total floor area is 800 square feet or smaller. (3) The height above grade does not exceed the applicable height limit provided in Section 6-563(b). || [6-566] The following section applies to ADUs that do not qualify as Class A or Class B ADUs. ... (b)(2) Subject to subsections (a)(3) and (b)(1), above, front yard setbacks shall be as follows: (A) R-6, R-10, R-12, R-15, D-1, M-R-A, M-R-B, M-R-O districts: At least 20 feet; ...
state_track_front.notes: Class A detached unit lists side/rear, size, height only. 6-563 (general requirements for Classes A/B/C) has no setback clause. The district-specific front setbacks (20/25/30/50 ft) and the 800 sf yield in 6-566(a)(3) apply only to Class C. No placement rule.

state_track_front.quote: One detached ADU, new construction with a proposed or existing single-family dwelling that complies with the following standards: (1) The lot on which the ADU is located does not contain another ADU, but may contain a JADU permitted pursuant to Section 8.124.110.B (2) Front yard setbacks consistent with the applicable zoning district to the extent such setbacks do not preclude development of an ADU. (3) The side and rear setbacks are at least four feet. (4) The total interior floor area is not more than eight hundred (800) square feet. (5) The height is sixteen (16) feet or less.

The yield is phrased 'to the extent such setbacks do not preclude development of an ADU' (not tied to 800 sf in words, but the unit is capped at 800 sf by (4)). Standard (non-streamlined) ADUs at 8.124.130(D) get the district front with no relief. 8.124.080 general requirements contain no placement or front rule.

state_track_front.quote: [B.3 Detached, New Construction (Single-Family)—ADUs] ... e. The ADU is located at least four feet from the side and rear lot lines, is no greater than eight hundred (800) adjusted square feet in floor area, and has a height in compliance with OMC section 17.3.4.(C)(4)(c). || [C] All Other ADUs. Any ADU that does not meet the standards for streamlined ADUs in Subsection B shall meet the following development standards and use restrictions: ... 4. The ADU meets all other applicable requirements of this code that do not involve discretionary review including, but not limited to, building height, setback, water channel setback, ...
state_track_front.notes: Streamlined (66323) section lists side/rear, size, height only. The requirement to meet all other code setbacks (C.4) applies only to non-streamlined ADUs. The chapter never uses the word 'front'. No placement rule.
state_track_front.source: ADU chapter read in full 2026-10-18 (corpus/orinda/adu-ordinance.txt) · FOR-1511

front_rule.citation: TC 17.010.110(B) (Ord. 885, 11-1-2023) - "The front of a corner lot is the narrowest dimension of the lot with street frontage"; this is the operative front declaration. 17.010.120(B) refers to a "corner side yard", confirming one front plus one street side. Street-side treatment: 17.040.020(D) gives all street frontage of any corner lot a 10 ft setback, which equals the 10 ft front yard setback in 17.040.020(A), so the numeric outcome is identical either way - this entry was previously labeled all_fronts on the strength of 17.040.020(D), but that is a setback rule, not a front declaration. Ch. 17.008 defines CORNER LOT as "a lot in the junction of and fronting on two or more intersecting streets" (locational, not operative) and never defines "front lot line"; 17.010.110(B) fills that gap. Caveat: 17.040.020 preamble is ambiguously drafted ("no accessory structure or building...") and per-district primary-dwelling setbacks were not traced.

residential_front_setback.citation: FTC § 17.076.070(A)(1) (RS-7.5): front + rear combined ≥ 30 ft, neither < 10 ft; § 17.080.070 (RS-6): combined ≥ 25 ft, neither < 6 ft
residential_front_setback.note: combined front+rear rule: the number is the front minimum, the rear absorbs the rest

state_track_front.quote: [(E)(1)(b)] Limited detached on lot with single-family. One or two detached, new-construction ADU on a lot with a proposed or existing single-family dwelling (in addition to any JADU that might otherwise be established on the lot under division (E)(1) above), if the detached ADU satisfies each of the following limitations: 1. The side- and rear-yard setbacks are at least four feet. 2. The total floor area is 1,200 square feet or smaller (based on interior livable space). 3. The peak height above grade does not exceed the applicable height limit in division (F)(2)(a) through (c) below. || [(G)] Specific ADU requirements. The following requirements apply only to Class 2 ADUs approved under division (E)(2) above. This subsection does not apply to Class 1 ADUs or JADUs approved under division (E)(1) above. ... (3)(a) ADUs that are subject to this division (G) must conform to four-foot side and rear setbacks. ADUs that are subject to this division (G) must conform to ten-foot front setbacks.
state_track_front.notes: Class 1 (statutorily regulated, Gov. Code 66323) detached unit runs to 1,200 sf locally (larger than the 800 sf state threshold). Division (F) (general requirements for Class 1 and 2) contains height, sprinklers, rental, etc. but no setback language. The 10-ft front and the 800 sf yield in (G)(1)(c) apply only to Class 2. No placement rule.
state_track_front.source: ADU chapter read in full 2026-10-18 (corpus/fairfax/adu-ordinance.txt) · FOR-1511

front_rule.citation: MMC 20.90.030(A)(12) - primary frontage by driveway/home orientation; remaining street frontage is the side yard

residential_front_setback.citation: MVMC § 20.16.040(C) (RS districts): exterior yards 15 ft
residential_front_setback.note: Mill Valley sets one exterior-yard number for all RS districts

state_track_front.quote: [20.90.040(A)(1)] As provided under Government Code Section 65852.2(e)(1), an owner shall not be required to submit an application for an ADU permit under subsection B below, and may instead seek building permit approval for the following types of units that are located within residential or mixeduse zones: ... c. New construction of detached ADUs meeting the requirements of Government Code Sections 65852.2(e)(1)(B) or 65852.2(e)(1)(D). || [20.90.050] Except for those ADUs approved under Section 20.90.040(A), an ADU shall comply with the following development standards. ... A.1. An ADU shall conform to all lot coverage, adjusted floor area, and setback regulations applicable to the zoning district in which the property is located, except in the following cases: a. ADUs or JADUs that are not required to obtain an ADU permit as provided under Section 20.90.040(A). b. Where the application of lot coverage, adjusted floor area, and setback violates Government Code Section 65852.2(c)(2)(C).
state_track_front.notes: HARD CALL (silent-by-exemption). Chapter still cites pre-2025 numbering (65852.2(e)(1)(B) = today's 66323(a)(2), 800 sf). The exempt-unit clause states no local standards at all; 20.90.050 (district setbacks with a yield by reference to 65852.2(c)(2)(C), today's 66321(b)(3)) is expressly disapplied for those units twice. BUT 20.90.030(A)(12), in the general requirements that apply to all ADUs, says units qualifying for reduced rear/side setbacks under 65852.2 on double-frontage or corner lots 'shall maintain the exterior yard setback for the primary frontage' (the opposite/remaining frontage being treated as rear/side). So on corner and through lots the district front on the primary frontage does reach the state-track unit (district_applies there); on interior lots the chapter is silent. No placement rule.
state_track_front.source: ADU chapter read in full 2026-10-18 (corpus/mill-valley/adu-ordinance.txt) · FOR-1511

front_rule.citation: SMC 10.88 - owner elects the front street line with Director concurrence

residential_front_setback.citation: SMC § 10.22.040 Table 10.22-2: front 0 ft in R-1-6, R-1-8, R-1-20; note 8: 10 ft where designated on the zoning map (§ 10.40.070E.4 special setback lines)

state_track_front.quote: [E.1.b] Limited Detached on Lot with Single-Family: One detached, new-construction ADU on a lot with a proposed or existing single-family dwelling, if the detached ADU satisfies each of the following limitations: i. The side- and rear-yard setbacks are at least four feet. ii. The total floor area is 800 square feet of livable space or smaller. iii. The peak height above grade does not exceed the applicable height limit in subsection F.2 of this section. || [G] Specific ADU Requirements. The following requirements apply only to Class 2 ADUs approved under subsection E.2 of this section. This subsection G does not apply to Class 1 ADUs or JADUs approved under subsection E.1 of this section. ... G.3.a ADUs that are subject to this subsection G must conform to four-foot side and rear setbacks, ADUs that are subject to this subsection G must conform to 10-foot front setbacks, subject to subsection G.1.c of this section.

placement_rule.quote: Historic District Protections. Any attached or detached ADU that is within the City of Sausalito Historic District (-H overlay district) must be located entirely behind the rear-most exterior wall of the primary dwelling and directly behind the primary dwelling.

state_track_front.notes: Class 1 (66323) detached unit lists side/rear, size, height only; subsection F (all classes) has no setback clause. The 10-ft front with the 800 sf yield (G.1.c) is Class 2 only. Placement rule G.10 applies only inside the -H historic overlay and is within subsection G, which 'does not apply to Class 1 ADUs' (express disapplication rather than a literal 'notwithstanding').
state_track_front.source: ADU chapter read in full 2026-10-18 (corpus/sausalito/adu-ordinance.txt) · FOR-1511

front_rule.citation: NMC 17.06.030 - on a corner lot the front line is the shorter of any two adjacent street lot lines

residential_front_setback.citation: NMC § 17.08.030 table: RS-10, RS-7, RS-5, RS-4, RM 20 ft; RS-40, RS-20 30 ft; block-average rule (note 3) may lower it

state_track_front.quote: [(C)(4)(b)] Except for conversions, a setback of four feet from the side and rear lot lines shall be required for each accessory dwelling unit or junior accessory dwelling unit. || [(C)(4)(c)] Except for conversions, accessory dwelling units shall comply with the front setback requirement of the underlying zoning district unless such setback would prevent the construction of an 800 square foot accessory dwelling unit in compliance with Government Code section 66323(a)(4) or any successor provisions. This subsection (C)(4)(c) does not apply to proposed accessory dwelling units described in and meeting the requirements of Government Code section 66323(a).
state_track_front.notes: HARD CALL (grant by front-specific disapplication). The chapter's only front-setback clause (district front + 800 sf yield) is expressly declared not to apply to 66323(a) units, and nothing else in the chapter imposes a front on them, so the local text affirmatively removes the front requirement for the state-track unit. Classified grant_none because the disapplication is specific to the front-setback subsection (contrast Contra Costa / Mill Valley, where the whole standards section is disapplied and I classified silent). Same 'does not apply to 66323(a)' pattern used for coverage (C)(3). No placement rule.
state_track_front.source: ADU chapter read in full 2026-10-18 (corpus/napa/adu-ordinance.txt) · FOR-1511

This type of ADU does not have a front yard setback.

Same sentence repeated for detached ADUs on multifamily lots at (F)(6). (F)(8) only defines which yard is 'front' on corner/double-frontage lots. No placement rule; entrance-orientation rule in (G) applies only to ADUs >800 sf.

state_track_front.quote: [D.1.b] Limited Detached on Lot with Single-Family. One detached, new-construction ADU on a lot with a proposed or existing single-family dwelling, if the detached ADU satisfies each of the following limitations: (1) The side- and rear-yard setbacks are at least four feet. (2) The total floor area is eight hundred square feet of livable space or smaller. (3) The peak height above grade does not exceed the applicable height limit in subsection E.2. below. || [F] Class 2 ADU Requirements. The following requirements apply only to class 2 ADUs approved under subsection D.2. above. This subsection F. does not apply to class 1 ADUs or JADUs approved under subsection D.1. above. ... 2.b. Front. ADUs that are subject to this subsection F. must conform to twenty-foot front setbacks, notwithstanding subsection F.1.c. above.
state_track_front.notes: Class 1 (Gov. Code 66323) detached unit lists side/rear, size, height only. Subsection E (general requirements for all classes) has no setback clause. The 20-ft front in F.2.b applies only to Class 2 and is expressly NOT subject to the 800 sf yield in F.1.c ('notwithstanding subsection F.1.c'), i.e. Class 2 units get no front relief at all. No placement rule (F.8 landscape screening is Class 2 only).

front_rule.citation: MPMC 16.04.405 - owner may elect the front lot line on corner lots

state_track_front.quote: [16.79.050 intro] 66323 Units need only comply with the development standards set forth in this subsection. ... (a)(2) One detached ADU. For a lot with an existing or proposed single-family dwelling, one detached, new construction ADU that meets all the following requirements: (A) Maximum Floor Area. The ADU shall not exceed 800 square feet of interior livable space. (B) Minimum Rear and Side Setbacks. Four feet. (C) Maximum Height: (i) 16 feet for a detached ADU on a lot with an existing or proposed single-family unit. (ii) 18 feet ... || [16.79.050(d)] No objective development or design standard shall be imposed on an ADU authorized by this section unless expressly authorized by Government Code Section 66323(b).
state_track_front.notes: 66323 Unit section lists size, side/rear, height only, and (d) bars imposing any other objective standard. The 'Front | N/A' cell at Table 16.79.060(1) is the JADU table, not this unit. The conditional-yield row ('Front setback per zoning district; setback must yield to the extent necessary to enable the construction of an 800-square-foot ADU with four-foot side- and rear-yard setbacks') is Table 16.79.070(1) for 66314 Units only. No placement rule.

The conditional-yield sentence at C.1.ii ('front setbacks ... shall not be imposed if they preclude a unit authorized by Government Code Section 66321(b)(3)') applies only to ADUs that do NOT meet C.1.i, so this is not mixed. front_rule.citation: SCMC 18.41.020 - corner lot front = the shorter lot line abutting a street; flag lots: interior line nearest and most parallel to the access street

residential_front_setback.citation: SCMC Table 18.04.030: RS-6 15 ft (1st story) / 19 ft (2nd story); RS-3 20 ft

state_track_front.quote: [UNCONDITIONAL] (F)(4)(b) Accessory dwelling units shall comply with lot coverage requirements, MFA, required front setbacks of the underlying zoning district, and natural state and open space requirements when applicable, as well as other applicable development standards, except that: ... and unless classified as a Statewide exemption ADU per subsection (F)(4)(c) of this section. | (F)(4)(e)(i) Detached accessory dwelling units must be set back a minimum of four (4) feet from rear and four (4) feet from the side property lines. Accessory dwelling units that are not classified as statewide exemption ADUs must meet the required front setback unless located within a legal, nonconforming structure. || [CONDITIONAL] (F)(4)(c) Statewide Exemption ADU. Notwithstanding the development standards set forth in subsection (F)(4)(b) of this section, if there is no alternative to constructing an accessory dwelling unit in accordance with the development standards listed in subsection (F)(4)(b) of this section, one (1) or more of these development standards may be waived only to the extent necessary to allow a Statewide exemption ADU of up to eight hundred (800) square feet with a maximum of sixteen (16) feet in height ..., with minimum four (4) foot side and four (4) foot rear yard setbacks. The front setback requirement may be reduced to the extent necessary so as not to preclude a Statewide exemption ADU and must not unduly constrain the creation of all types of accessory dwelling units. | Table 18.23.210(E)(4) Detached ADUs, Statewide Exemption column: Front | May be reduced to 0' if no other location is feasible
state_track_front.notes: Genuinely mixed. Three sentences carve statewide-exemption ADUs out of the front setback unconditionally ('unless classified as a Statewide exemption ADU' in (F)(4)(b) and (e)(iii); 'ADUs that are not classified as statewide exemption ADUs must meet the required front setback' in (e)(i)), while (F)(4)(c) and both new-construction tables make the relief conditional ('only to the extent necessary', 'if no other location is feasible', applicant 'must also demonstrate that an ADU cannot be constructed in accordance with applicable development standards'). The 'Front | None | None' row is the conversion/same-footprint table, not new construction. (F)(5)(a) (ADUs over detached garages) also exempts statewide-exemption ADUs from the front; its cross-reference to 18.04.030(H) (detached garage in front half of lot) is a garage rule, not an ADU placement rule.
state_track_front.source: ADU chapter read in full 2026-10-18 (corpus/san-carlos/adu-ordinance.txt) · FOR-1511

front_rule.citation: SMMC 27.04.300(a) - on a corner lot the owner may elect either street property line as the front; through lots: both street lines are fronts (27.04.275(d))

residential_front_setback.citation: SMMC § 27.18.070(a): R1-B and R1-C 15 ft; R1-A 25 ft; garages 20 ft (b)

state_track_front.quote: [27.19.060(d)(3)] A minimum setback from the front lot line, as required in the lot's underlying zone district, shall be required for all New Construction ADUs not meeting the criteria set forth in subsection (1) above, including ADUs constructed above an existing garage. No setback is required for a State Exempt ADU. || [27.19.020(6)] "State Exempt ADU" means an accessory dwelling unit that is created pursuant to Government Code Section 66323.
state_track_front.notes: Unconditional. The sentence literally reads 'No setback is required' (not 'no front setback'), but it sits inside the front-setback paragraph (d)(3) while (d)(2) separately requires 4-ft side/rear 'for all new ADU construction'; the multifamily twin at 27.19.070(e)(2) says it explicitly: 'No front setback is required for a New Construction Detached State Exempt ADU.' (d)(1) also waives all setbacks for a detached ADU in the rear one-third of an R1 lot that meets Chapter 27.70. No placement rule.

overrides.description: A lot that exceeds the corner-lot dimension thresholds is not a corner lot and is deemed to have two front property lines. state_track_front.quote: [(h)(3) Location. ADUs shall be located subject to the following setbacks, and in conformance with any easements and building envelopes:] (i) Front Yard Setback: As established by the base zoning district, unless compliance with the setback would not permit an ADU of eight hundred (800) square feet, meeting applicable height standards, with four-foot side and rear yard setbacks. (ii) Side and Rear Yard Setbacks: Four (4) feet.
state_track_front.notes: No separate 66323 section (chapter still cites 65852.2); (h)(3) applies to all ADUs. Straight shield wording. The 'in conformance with any easements and building envelopes' clause is a site-constraint, not a front-yard exclusion. No placement rule.
